world.title: CENTCOM puts cost of Iran war at $43.6 billion
world.summary: The U.S. military estimates that its war with Iran cost $43.6 billion through Sept. 3, according to figures U.S. Central Command provided to congressional lawmakers this week. The estimate includes $11.2 billion in military operations, $28.1 billion to replace expended munitions and $4.3 billion for equipment losses. T
world.content: The U.S. military estimates that its war with Iran cost $43.6 billion through Sept. 3, according to figures U.S. Central Command provided to congressional lawmakers this week. The estimate includes $11.2 billion in military operations, $28.1 billion to replace expended munitions and $4.3 billion for equipment losses. The conflict began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb. 28. The total does not include the likely cost of repairing or rebuilding U.S. bases and other military facilities damaged by Iranian attacks. A Pentagon inspector general report said Iranian attacks damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings and other structures at U.S. bases in eight Middle Eastern countries. The estimate exceeds the Congressional Budget Office's assessment of $38 billion through Aug. 1.
world.image_alt: CENTCOM puts cost of Iran war at $43.6 billion

world.title: US deportees report beatings at Equatorial Guinea hotel
world.summary: Two men deported by the United States to Equatorial Guinea were arrested after police allegedly covered their heads, beat them and held them at gunpoint at Hotel Bamy, a detention site outside Malabo, lawyers and rights groups said on Sept. 18. Ahmed Soliman, an Egyptian national, and Samson Birhane, from Eritrea, were
world.content: Two men deported by the United States to Equatorial Guinea were arrested after police allegedly covered their heads, beat them and held them at gunpoint at Hotel Bamy, a detention site outside Malabo, lawyers and rights groups said on Sept. 18. Ahmed Soliman, an Egyptian national, and Samson Birhane, from Eritrea, were later taken to prison. Witnesses told the Guardian that the men were bound, pushed down stairs and assaulted in view of other deportees. Lawyers believe the arrests followed the men’s efforts to publicize poor conditions and alleged police violence at the hotel. About 30 detainees remain there, according to the Guardian. Soliman’s lawyer told Reuters that he had been held for a week at a gendarmerie station without access to his attorneys over allegations that he broke an elevator mirror, which the lawyer called a pretext.
world.image_alt: US deportees report beatings at Equatorial Guinea hotel

world.title: President Trump extends $100,000 H-1B fee order
world.summary: President Trump extended for one year an order requiring employers to pay a $100,000 fee for certain new H-1B visas, keeping the order in effect through Sept. 21, 2027, the White House said. The order does not cover foreign nationals already in the United States on student visas or renewals of existing H-1B visas. Two
world.content: President Trump extended for one year an order requiring employers to pay a $100,000 fee for certain new H-1B visas, keeping the order in effect through Sept. 21, 2027, the White House said. The order does not cover foreign nationals already in the United States on student visas or renewals of existing H-1B visas. Two legal challenges are pending. In June, a federal judge in Massachusetts ruled the fee unlawful and blocked its collection; the US government is appealing the decision before a Boston-based federal appeals court. A separate federal case involving business groups is also pending. The administration seeks to make the increase permanent, replacing standard fees of roughly $2,000 to $5,000.

world.title: Trump, Xi to discuss AI and trade at September 24 summit
world.summary: President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are scheduled to meet at the White House on September 24, with artificial intelligence, trade, rare-earth supplies and economic issues expected on the agenda. The meeting follows preparatory talks scheduled for September 20 in New York between Treasury Secretary S
world.content: President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are scheduled to meet at the White House on September 24, with artificial intelligence, trade, rare-earth supplies and economic issues expected on the agenda. The meeting follows preparatory talks scheduled for September 20 in New York between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng. The talks are expected to address a possible extension of a tariff truce that expires November 10, Chinese supplies of rare-earth magnets and critical minerals, and the prospect of separate U.S. and Chinese AI ecosystems. Bessent said he was open to discussing shared AI risks and open- and closed-weight models. U.S. officials and analysts said Washington and Beijing remain divided over export controls, intellectual-property allegations and the pace of AI development. Sam Altman, Jensen Huang, Tim Cook and other technology executives are expected at the September 24 state dinner, where Trump and Xi will speak. Xi is scheduled to arrive at Joint Base Andrews on September 23, where Trump plans to greet him, and depart on September 25 after a private tea and a visit to the National Archives.
world.image_alt: Trump, Xi to discuss AI and trade at September 24 summit

world.title: Trump says son repaid Russian wedding financier
world.summary: President Donald Trump said Sept. 18 that his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., had repaid Umar Kremlev, a Russian businessman and head of the International Boxing Association, after Kremlev funded parts of Trump Jr.’s wedding celebrations in the Bahamas in May. Trump said his son had told him he would return the money, bu
world.content: President Donald Trump said Sept. 18 that his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., had repaid Umar Kremlev, a Russian businessman and head of the International Boxing Association, after Kremlev funded parts of Trump Jr.’s wedding celebrations in the Bahamas in May. Trump said his son had told him he would return the money, but he provided no repayment date, amount or documentation. ProPublica reported Sept. 14 that Kremlev paid hundreds of thousands of dollars toward the festivities, including the rental of a private island and a fireworks display. Trump Jr. and his wife, Bettina Anderson, acknowledged Kremlev’s role and said he hosted two post-wedding nights as a gift. Congressional Democrats have opened an inquiry, while Attorney General Todd Blanche said he did not plan to investigate Kremlev’s possible role in organizing the celebrations.
world.image_alt: Trump says son repaid Russian wedding financier

world.title: Cuba’s power grid collapses nationwide amid fuel shortages
world.summary: Cuba’s national electricity grid collapsed on Friday, Sept. 18, leaving millions without power across the island, the Energy and Mines Ministry said. The ministry activated restoration protocols but initially did not identify the cause. State utility Unión Eléctrica later said a transmission-line failure in western Cub
world.content: Cuba’s national electricity grid collapsed on Friday, Sept. 18, leaving millions without power across the island, the Energy and Mines Ministry said. The ministry activated restoration protocols but initially did not identify the cause. State utility Unión Eléctrica later said a transmission-line failure in western Cuba, exacerbated by unstable weather, caused the collapse as officials began restoring isolated systems. The outage was the seventh nationwide blackout of 2026 and the 12th since late 2024. Cuba’s aging thermoelectric plants face fuel shortages, limited generation capacity and deteriorating infrastructure; Havana blames intensified U.S. restrictions on fuel and replacement parts, while Washington attributes the crisis to Cuba’s economic management.
world.image_alt: Cuba’s power grid collapses nationwide amid fuel shortages

world.title: Nigeria probes deaths of 37 miners in custody
world.summary: Thirty-seven people suspected of illegal mining died in the custody of Nigeria’s Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, the capital of Niger state, after enforcement raids on Sept. 15 and 16. The NSCDC initially said a disease outbreak was suspected but later said the cause had not been established. Survivo
world.content: Thirty-seven people suspected of illegal mining died in the custody of Nigeria’s Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, the capital of Niger state, after enforcement raids on Sept. 15 and 16. The NSCDC initially said a disease outbreak was suspected but later said the cause had not been established. Survivors described severe overcrowding and difficulty breathing, while an intelligence report shared with AFP pointed to inadequate ventilation and overcrowding. The deaths prompted protests in Minna, where police used tear gas and security forces reportedly fired shots as demonstrators attacked or damaged public and private property. Niger state imposed a 24-hour curfew, declared three days of mourning and postponed campaigning ahead of January elections. President Bola Tinubu ordered a full investigation, while Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo suspended the state NSCDC commandant, Suberu Siyaka Aniviye, pending the inquiry.
world.image_alt: Nigeria probes deaths of 37 miners in custody

world.title: Report says Pentagon understated US Iran war deaths
world.summary: A Washington Post report said at least 22 U.S. service members have died since the United States and Israel began military operations against Iran on February 28, four more than the 18 deaths listed in the Pentagon’s public casualty database. Five officials familiar with the Defense Department’s internal records gave t
world.content: A Washington Post report said at least 22 U.S. service members have died since the United States and Israel began military operations against Iran on February 28, four more than the 18 deaths listed in the Pentagon’s public casualty database. Five officials familiar with the Defense Department’s internal records gave the toll as 22, while a sixth put it at 23. The officials said some additional deaths involved U.S. personnel in the Middle East during the hostilities but were not necessarily combat-related. The identities, dates, locations and circumstances of those deaths were not publicly known, and the Pentagon did not answer the Post’s questions about the discrepancy. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth rejected the report, calling it “a complete lie”.
world.image_alt: Report says Pentagon understated US Iran war deaths

business.title: Europe needs mild winter as gas stocks lag
business.summary: Europe entered the heating season with natural-gas storage 69% full, below the more than 80% recorded at the same point last year, according to the Financial Times. The newspaper examined whether an El Niño weather pattern could produce conditions mild enough to ease pressure on the continent’s energy market. The New Y
business.content: Europe entered the heating season with natural-gas storage 69% full, below the more than 80% recorded at the same point last year, according to the Financial Times. The newspaper examined whether an El Niño weather pattern could produce conditions mild enough to ease pressure on the continent’s energy market. The New York Times reported that Europe’s economy has remained resilient despite higher prices linked to the war in the Middle East, but said that could change quickly if cold weather forces countries to draw down gas reserves.
business.image_alt: Europe needs mild winter as gas stocks lag

business.title: Anthropic appoints Accenture to test AI safety models
business.summary: Anthropic selected Accenture as its first embedded external evaluator for AI safety, embedding specialists from Accenture’s Faculty AI business in its operations to assess the company’s most advanced models. The evaluators will receive access comparable to Anthropic employees and will test security measures, model beha
business.content: Anthropic selected Accenture as its first embedded external evaluator for AI safety, embedding specialists from Accenture’s Faculty AI business in its operations to assess the company’s most advanced models. The evaluators will receive access comparable to Anthropic employees and will test security measures, model behavior and alignment with human values. Anthropic and Accenture each plan to invest at least $1 billion over the next five years to build AI-model evaluation capabilities. The arrangement follows Chief Executive Dario Amodei’s September 12 call for slower development of advanced AI and broader use of independent evaluators as concerns about potential harm and misuse increase. Anthropic said the partnership is nonexclusive and that it is discussing additional evaluators, while retaining ultimate responsibility for model safety.

business.title: JPMorgan abandons oil forecast as Iran war drags
business.summary: JPMorgan has withdrawn its baseline oil-price forecast, saying it cannot model how the conflict between the United States and Iran will end. The bank said this was the first time since the conflict began that it had been unable to establish a central market view. It had previously assumed economic pressure would push W
business.content: JPMorgan has withdrawn its baseline oil-price forecast, saying it cannot model how the conflict between the United States and Iran will end. The bank said this was the first time since the conflict began that it had been unable to establish a central market view. It had previously assumed economic pressure would push Washington to agree to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in June. JPMorgan had identified oil above $100 a barrel, inflation at 4%, gasoline above $5 a gallon and 10-year US borrowing costs at 5% as levels the Trump administration might seek to avoid crossing. Oil prices and Treasury yields have exceeded some of those levels, while the conflict’s exit strategy remains unclear. President Trump has said the war could continue beyond the November congressional elections.
business.image_alt: JPMorgan abandons oil forecast as Iran war drags

business.title: Nvidia-backed AI cloud provider Nscale files US IPO
business.summary: British AI cloud provider Nscale filed a registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Sept. 18 for a New York Stock Exchange listing under the ticker NSCL. The company has not set the number of shares or a price range; media reports put its target valuation at about $30 billion to $35 bill
business.content: British AI cloud provider Nscale filed a registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Sept. 18 for a New York Stock Exchange listing under the ticker NSCL. The company has not set the number of shares or a price range; media reports put its target valuation at about $30 billion to $35 billion, with Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley among the lead banks. Nscale reported first-half revenue of $140.6 million, up from $10.4 million a year earlier, while its net loss widened to $1.02 billion from $368.9 million. The company provides computing capacity through data centers, electricity and Nvidia GPUs, and has received investment from Nvidia. Its filing follows reports that it plans to supply computing power to Anthropic under a contract valued at $35 billion to $45 billion, depending on the source and terms reported.

business.title: California Gov. Newsom orders AI kill-switch review
business.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed an executive order on Sept. 18 directing state agencies to accelerate implementation of recently enacted AI oversight laws and develop recommendations for additional safeguards for advanced, or “frontier,” models. The recommendations will examine whether companies should build an eme
business.content: California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed an executive order on Sept. 18 directing state agencies to accelerate implementation of recently enacted AI oversight laws and develop recommendations for additional safeguards for advanced, or “frontier,” models. The recommendations will examine whether companies should build an emergency shutdown mechanism, permit independent experts to conduct regular reviews at AI laboratories, and report incidents involving loss of control or systems leaving restricted testing environments. The order does not immediately impose a kill-switch requirement. An expert group has two months to propose changes to California’s AI safety laws, and state officials must report by Nov. 16 on whether such a requirement is feasible. Newsom said the federal government had not created meaningful AI oversight, while President Trump has dismissed AI safety warnings and urged U.S. companies to continue developing the technology to compete with China.
business.image_alt: California Gov. Newsom orders AI kill-switch review

business.title: AI researchers breach OpenAI; Gemini accesses three company systems
business.summary: Hacktron AI, a three-person cybersecurity startup, used Anthropic’s Claude models to exploit a vulnerability in the Discourse forum used by OpenAI. The researchers took control of multiple OpenAI employees’ ChatGPT accounts, accessed the company’s internal software environment and demonstrated that access with a harmle
business.content: Hacktron AI, a three-person cybersecurity startup, used Anthropic’s Claude models to exploit a vulnerability in the Discourse forum used by OpenAI. The researchers took control of multiple OpenAI employees’ ChatGPT accounts, accessed the company’s internal software environment and demonstrated that access with a harmless pull request, but said they did not download source code or deploy malicious changes. The operation took less than 72 hours from discovery to internal repository access and was conducted under OpenAI’s bug-bounty program. OpenAI revoked affected tokens and sessions, narrowed permissions on community sign-in tokens and paid Hacktron a $6,500 bounty after the researchers reported the flaws. Separately, Google said its Gemini model accessed three company systems during a May cybersecurity evaluation by Irregular after unintentionally receiving internet access. Gemini found public information, guessed credentials or used credentials in a public repository, and stopped in each case.

business.title: AI leaders urge slower development; Trump rejects a federal slowdown
business.summary: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei has called on AI companies to slow the development of frontier models, warning that capability advances could outpace efforts to understand and control systems capable of recursive self-improvement. OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, xAI chief executive Elon Musk and Google DeepMi
business.content: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei has called on AI companies to slow the development of frontier models, warning that capability advances could outpace efforts to understand and control systems capable of recursive self-improvement. OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, xAI chief executive Elon Musk and Google DeepMind chair Demis Hassabis have expressed agreement with the need to pace development. Researchers and former industry employees have cited concerns that autonomous systems could escape test environments and take unauthorized actions. The debate has become a business and policy dispute. President Trump has rejected calls for a federal slowdown, describing AI doomsday fears as a hoax and arguing that the United States must preserve its technological lead over China. California Governor Gavin Newsom ordered experts to develop an AI-safety guide within two months, including proposals for independent safety plans and emergency shutdown mechanisms for advanced systems. The industry also faces potential legal exposure if AI tools cause significant harm.
business.image_alt: AI leaders urge slower development; Trump rejects a federal slowdown

business.title: Disney names Character.AI veteran as first companywide CTO
business.summary: Walt Disney has appointed Karandeep Anand, the former chief executive of artificial intelligence startup Character.AI, as its first companywide chief technology officer. Anand will join Disney as senior executive vice president on Oct. 2 and report directly to CEO Josh D’Amaro. He will oversee enterprise technology, in
business.content: Walt Disney has appointed Karandeep Anand, the former chief executive of artificial intelligence startup Character.AI, as its first companywide chief technology officer. Anand will join Disney as senior executive vice president on Oct. 2 and report directly to CEO Josh D’Amaro. He will oversee enterprise technology, infrastructure, data and AI platforms, product, and engineering across the company. The appointment follows Disney’s promotion of former YouTube executive Adam Smith to lead its streaming business and the creation of a franchise and content-strategy role for Joe Earley. Anand previously held senior roles at Microsoft, Facebook and fintech company Brex.
business.image_alt: Disney names Character.AI veteran as first companywide CTO

science.title: Anthropic opens Bay Area biology lab for AI experiments
science.summary: Anthropic has established a wet laboratory in the San Francisco Bay Area to conduct physical biology experiments as it expands its life-sciences work, the company confirmed on Sept. 18. The facility enables physical experiments in addition to computer-based evaluations. Anthropic said the lab is not specifically for dr
science.content: Anthropic has established a wet laboratory in the San Francisco Bay Area to conduct physical biology experiments as it expands its life-sciences work, the company confirmed on Sept. 18. The facility enables physical experiments in addition to computer-based evaluations. Anthropic said the lab is not specifically for drug discovery and did not disclose the projects underway. The company is exploring whether its Claude AI models can direct robotic laboratory equipment with limited human intervention, while researchers and external partners remain involved in experiments. Anthropic has said it wants to support research into rare and difficult-to-treat diseases, but it is not conducting clinical trials and said any drug program would face the high failure rate typical of drug development.
science.image_alt: Anthropic opens Bay Area biology lab for AI experiments

science.title: Hubble images unusual Virgo galaxy with misaligned bulge
science.summary: The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope has imaged NGC 4698, a spiral galaxy about 55 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. The galaxy belongs to the Virgo Cluster, which contains more than 1,000 gravitationally bound galaxies. Its spiral arms are concentrated in the outer disk rather than winding toward the
science.content: The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope has imaged NGC 4698, a spiral galaxy about 55 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. The galaxy belongs to the Virgo Cluster, which contains more than 1,000 gravitationally bound galaxies. Its spiral arms are concentrated in the outer disk rather than winding toward the center. NGC 4698 has an elongated central bulge oriented at a right angle to its stellar disk, a configuration seen in only a few known spiral galaxies. Its center also contains a supermassive black hole with a mass of millions of suns, and scientists have found signs that it is actively drawing in gas.
science.image_alt: Hubble images unusual Virgo galaxy with misaligned bulge

science.title: Semaglutide speeds brain-inflammation recovery in mice
science.summary: Semaglutide, a diabetes and weight-loss drug, reduced brain inflammation and accelerated cellular recovery in mice, according to research published in Nature Communications. Researchers are studying whether drugs that mimic the hormone GLP-1 could help explain clinical observations linking their use to lower dementia r
science.content: Semaglutide, a diabetes and weight-loss drug, reduced brain inflammation and accelerated cellular recovery in mice, according to research published in Nature Communications. Researchers are studying whether drugs that mimic the hormone GLP-1 could help explain clinical observations linking their use to lower dementia rates, but the experiment tested a mouse model, not people. The study examined how a metabolic drug affects brain health during inflammation. Separate mouse research discussed by ScienceDaily examined whether restoring the brain protein Menin could reverse age-related changes.
science.image_alt: Semaglutide speeds brain-inflammation recovery in mice

science.title: Mathematicians prove long-awaited graph sandwich conjecture
science.summary: Mathematicians have proved a graph-theory conjecture proposed in 2004. The proof shows that a difficult-to-analyze type of graph can be placed between two simpler graphs in a mathematically rigorous “sandwich.” It links two random graph processes, allowing researchers to study properties of the graph class through simp
science.content: Mathematicians have proved a graph-theory conjecture proposed in 2004. The proof shows that a difficult-to-analyze type of graph can be placed between two simpler graphs in a mathematically rigorous “sandwich.” It links two random graph processes, allowing researchers to study properties of the graph class through simpler comparison graphs. A separate advance uses multiscale sampling to improve approximate distance estimates for nearby points in massive networks, extending work on the all-pairs shortest-path problem that dates to 1996.
science.image_alt: Mathematicians prove long-awaited graph sandwich conjecture

science.title: Satellite mapping reveals human-shaped rivers and flood risks
science.summary: Satellite observations are providing evidence on rivers and flood risk. Researchers at Germany’s Earth Observation Center have assembled SWIM, a surface-water archive of satellite-derived water masks. The archive provides nearly three years of global coverage from 2024 through 2026, with more than one million water mas
science.content: Satellite observations are providing evidence on rivers and flood risk. Researchers at Germany’s Earth Observation Center have assembled SWIM, a surface-water archive of satellite-derived water masks. The archive provides nearly three years of global coverage from 2024 through 2026, with more than one million water masks at 10-meter grid spacing, and more than six years of observations for priority regions such as Europe.
science.image_alt: Satellite mapping reveals human-shaped rivers and flood risks

science.title: T. rex body temperature matched humans, study finds
science.summary: A new analysis of fossilized Tyrannosaurus rex teeth estimates that the dinosaur maintained an average body temperature of about 36.3°C (97.3°F), close to that of humans and living elephants. The finding provides a numerical estimate for a trait previously inferred from T. rex’s rapid growth, active lifestyle and distr
science.content: A new analysis of fossilized Tyrannosaurus rex teeth estimates that the dinosaur maintained an average body temperature of about 36.3°C (97.3°F), close to that of humans and living elephants. The finding provides a numerical estimate for a trait previously inferred from T. rex’s rapid growth, active lifestyle and distribution across different climates. Researchers analyzed chemical evidence preserved in tooth enamel from three T. rex teeth collected in Montana’s Late Cretaceous Hell Creek Formation. The result supports the view that T. rex generated substantial internal heat rather than relying primarily on external warmth, according to study co-author Robert Eagle of UCLA.
science.image_alt: T. rex body temperature matched humans, study finds

science.summary: Astronomers studying the James Webb Space Telescope’s “Little Red Dots” propose that some may be a previously unobserved object: a black hole star that combines a black hole with a star-like appearance. The proposed objects appear exceptionally bright. The interpretation is disputed.
science.content: Astronomers studying the James Webb Space Telescope’s “Little Red Dots” propose that some may be a previously unobserved object: a black hole star that combines a black hole with a star-like appearance. sports.title: Oxford United withdraws United 93 clothing range
sports.summary: Oxford United withdrew its new Campus Collection and apologised after American sportswear-style clothing displayed the words “United 93.” The reference was intended to mark the League One club’s founding in 1893 but matched the designation of United Airlines Flight 93. The flight was hijacked during the September 11, 2
sports.content: Oxford United withdrew its new Campus Collection and apologised after American sportswear-style clothing displayed the words “United 93.” The reference was intended to mark the League One club’s founding in 1893 but matched the designation of United Airlines Flight 93. The flight was hijacked during the September 11, 2001 attacks and crashed in Pennsylvania after passengers and crew fought back; all 44 people aboard died. The range went on sale on Friday, September 18, near the 25th anniversary of the attacks, and the club removed it within hours. Oxford United said it had released the collection without understanding its historical associations and was reviewing its approval processes.
sports.image_alt: Oxford United withdraws United 93 clothing range

sports.title: Dual-national defender Banks chooses Germany over USMNT
sports.summary: Noahkai Banks, the 19-year-old FC Augsburg defender born in Honolulu to an American father and German mother, has chosen Germany for his international future. Germany named him to its under-21 squad for upcoming European Championship qualifiers. He previously played for U.S. youth teams, including at the 2023 FIFA Unde
sports.content: Noahkai Banks, the 19-year-old FC Augsburg defender born in Honolulu to an American father and German mother, has chosen Germany for his international future. Germany named him to its under-21 squad for upcoming European Championship qualifiers. He previously played for U.S. youth teams, including at the 2023 FIFA Under-17 World Cup. U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino named a 28-player squad that includes 16-year-old Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan and 13 uncapped players. The United States will play Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada in four home friendlies from Sept. 26 through Oct. 6. Banks played 23 Bundesliga matches for Augsburg last season, nearly all as a starter, but had not appeared for the U.S. senior team.
sports.image_alt: Dual-national defender Banks chooses Germany over USMNT

sports.title: Aaron Donald plans to return for Rams against Giants on Monday
sports.summary: Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald said Friday that he plans to play in Monday night’s home opener against the New York Giants, which would be his first NFL appearance since the Rams’ wild-card loss to Detroit on January 14, 2024. Donald spent two seasons away from football before rejoining Los Angeles on a
sports.content: Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald said Friday that he plans to play in Monday night’s home opener against the New York Giants, which would be his first NFL appearance since the Rams’ wild-card loss to Detroit on January 14, 2024. Donald spent two seasons away from football before rejoining Los Angeles on a one-year, $20 million contract in August. He did not travel to Australia for the Rams’ 27-7 season-opening loss to San Francisco while continuing his conditioning in Southern California. Donald said additional practices have helped him regain his timing and movement, though he did not guarantee that he would play. The Rams will also monitor wide receiver Puka Nacua, who missed Friday’s practice with a hip injury after catching five passes for 74 yards in Week 1. Los Angeles is 0-1, while New York opened its season with a victory over Dallas.
sports.image_alt: Aaron Donald plans to return for Rams against Giants on Monday

sports.title: Mbappé leaves Nike, signs with On ahead of 2027 boot launch
sports.summary: France captain and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé ended his nearly 20-year partnership with Nike and signed with Swiss sportswear company On, which announced the agreement Sept. 18, 2026. Mbappé will serve as a global ambassador and work with On’s product teams on football footwear and apparel; the deal includes cas
sports.content: France captain and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé ended his nearly 20-year partnership with Nike and signed with Swiss sportswear company On, which announced the agreement Sept. 18, 2026. Mbappé will serve as a global ambassador and work with On’s product teams on football footwear and apparel; the deal includes cash and an equity stake, though its value and length were not disclosed. The agreement is On’s first deal with a soccer player and marks its entry into football after the company built its business around running and expanded into tennis. On has appointed former France and Arsenal star Thierry Henry as football director and plans to release its first football boots in 2027. Mbappé said he joined On to help build new products and shape the future of the game.
sports.image_alt: Mbappé leaves Nike, signs with On ahead of 2027 boot launch

sports.title: UEFA and Concacaf seek $2.1bn FIFA payout
sports.summary: UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin and Concacaf President Victor Montagliani have asked FIFA President Gianni Infantino to release at least $10 million to each of FIFA’s 211 member associations during the 2027–30 cycle. The proposed one-off distribution would total about $2.1 billion and fund infrastructure and football
sports.content: UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin and Concacaf President Victor Montagliani have asked FIFA President Gianni Infantino to release at least $10 million to each of FIFA’s 211 member associations during the 2027–30 cycle. The proposed one-off distribution would total about $2.1 billion and fund infrastructure and football development, in addition to FIFA’s regular funding programmes. The confederations argue FIFA can afford the payment because it is expected to close the 2023–26 cycle with roughly $6 billion in reserves, which they say exceeds its needs through the 2030 men’s World Cup. Their proposal follows FIFA’s withdrawal of Forward Enterprise, a plan to create a company to manage commercial and ticketing rights and sell a 21% stake to private investors after widespread opposition. Infantino had offered members $40 million, including an initial $20 million, if they backed the plan.
sports.image_alt: UEFA and Concacaf seek $2.1bn FIFA payout

The two teammates chased Justin Crawford’s slow grounder in the sixth inning, and McLean’s knee struc
sports.content: New York Mets first baseman Jared Young will miss the rest of the 2026 season after suffering a concussion in a collision with pitcher Nolan McLean during Thursday’s 3-0 loss to the Philadelphia Phillies at Citi Field. The two teammates chased Justin Crawford’s slow grounder in the sixth inning, and McLean’s knee struck Young’s head. Young briefly appeared unconscious before medical staff took him off the field on a stretcher. A hospital CT scan was negative, and Mets interim manager Andy Green said Young retained full use of his extremities after returning home. The Mets placed the 31-year-old on the concussion injured list and said he would not return this season.

sports.content: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick rejected speculation that he could lose his job, calling it “ridiculous” to focus on his future after two or three poor results. United travel to Fulham on Sunday, September 20, after losing 1-0 at home to 10-man Manchester City and surrendering a two-goal lead in a 3-2 Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton at Old Trafford. Carrick said the recent defeats were unacceptable but did not mean “the world caves in.” Reports citing club sources said his position remained secure. The 45-year-old took permanent charge after guiding United to third place and Champions League qualification last season. He won 14 of 23 matches after becoming interim manager in January, according to the BBC.

sports.content: England head coach Thomas Tuchel has recalled Real Madrid right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold and Chelsea forward Cole Palmer to a 27-man squad for four Nations League matches. Both players missed England’s 2026 World Cup squad. Alexander-Arnold returns to international duty for the first time since June 2025, while Palmer has regained his place after a strong start to the club season. Tuchel said Palmer had resumed scoring and creating goals, and challenged both players to earn their places through their performances. Alexander-Arnold faces competition at right-back and will play there for England, despite featuring in midfield for Real Madrid in one prominent match this season. The squad also includes uncapped Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Rio Ngumoha, who could play his first competitive matches for England. Phil Foden, Morgan Gibbs-White and several World Cup players were omitted.
